answer:
Standard Precautions are the minimum infection prevention practices that apply to all patient care, regardless of the patient's suspected or confirmed infection status, in any setting where healthcare is delivered (Data/the-national-infection-prevention-and-control-guidelines-for-acute-healthcare-facilities---2017.pdf | Page: 13).

The purpose of Standard Precautions is to reduce the risk of transmission of pathogens (bacterium, virus, fungi or other microorganisms) from both recognized and unrecognized sources in the healthcare setting for the prevention and control of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). This applies to all staff involved in the delivery of patient care (Data/national-ipc-guidelines-for-chs_on-moh-website_23april.pdf | Page: 24). These practices are designed to both protect healthcare professionals (HCPs) and prevent them from spreading infections among patients, especially those involving blood-borne pathogens (Data/the-national-infection-prevention-and-control-guidelines-for-acute-healthcare-facilities---2017.pdf | Page: 13).

Standard Precautions include:
*   Hand hygiene (Data/the-national-infection-prevention-and-control-guidelines-for-acute-healthcare-facilities---2017.pdf | Page: 13)
*   Use of personal protective equipment (e.g., gloves, gowns, masks) (Data/the-national-infection-prevention-and-control-guidelines-for-acute-healthcare-facilities---2017.pdf | Page: 13)
*   Safe injection practices (Data/the-national-infection-prevention-and-control-guidelines-for-acute-healthcare-facilities---2017.pdf | Page: 13)

Specific examples of practices included under Standard Precautions are:
*   Personal Protective Equipment: Clothing or equipment worn by staff for protection against hazards (Data/the-national-infection-prevention-and-control-guidelines-for-acute-healthcare-facilities---2017.pdf | Page: 21)
*   Sterilization: Using specialized cleansing techniques to destroy all living microorganisms, such as pathogenic or saprophytic bacteria, vegetative forms, and spores (Data/the-national-infection-prevention-and-control-guidelines-for-acute-healthcare-facilities---2017.pdf | Page: 21)

*   **Policies and Standards:** Principles include policies for environmental cleaning and equipment decontamination, waste and linen management standards, and an assurance that these policies are well implemented (Data/national-ipc-guidelines-for-long-term-care-facilities_2021_revised_2nd-edition_moh-website.pdf | Page: 108).
*   **Regular Cleaning:** Wards should be cleaned regularly as part of a general programme of environmental hygiene (Data/national-ipc-guidelines-for-long-term-care-facilities_2021_revised_2nd-edition_moh-website.pdf | Page: 108).
*   **Hand Hygiene:** Adequate hand hygiene facilities and alcohol-based handrub should be available for staff and visitor hand decontamination before and after contact with the resident or their immediate environment (Data/national-ipc-guidelines-for-long-term-care-facilities_2021_revised_2nd-edition_moh-website.pdf | Page: 108).
*   **Planning and Monitoring:** The cleaning programme should include monitoring of cleaning practices so that improvement initiatives may be planned to meet best practices (Data/national-ipc-guidelines-for-chs_on-moh-website_23april.pdf | Page: 19).
*   **Foundation of the Plan:** The environmental hygiene plan must be based on current scientific knowledge, accepted practice guidelines, and relevant laws and regulations (Data/national-cleaning-standards-for-acute-healthcare-facilities_final-2024.pdf | Page: 10).
